facts.text: Redding was named after Benjamin Redding, a Central Pacific Railroad land agent who bought property in 1868, and the town grew around the railroad terminus that reached the area in 1872.
The city sits on the Sacramento River, 162 miles north of Sacramento and 120 miles south of Oregon’s border.
Redding’s warm summer nights are a result of its distance from maritime influences, giving it a climate distinct from southern California.
Shasta State Historic Park offers a California history field‑trip experience right in Redding’s backyard.
Vina Vineyard, named 2023 “Golden State Winery of the Year,” produces rosés and rare varietals like Trebbiano and Assyrtiko in downtown Redding.
Redding is the county seat of Shasta County and serves as the economic and cultural capital of the Shasta Cascade region of Northern California.
